page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The allocation consists of 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory footprint totals 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. The platform includes no physical GPU accelerators and zero local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file persistence. Baseline network throughput is rated at 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight an operational divergence between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests register in the lower quartile, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1109.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0, constrained by the conservative 2.5 GHz clock speed. Parallelized workloads demonstrate more robust capacity, scoring 23532.01 in multi-core stress-ng, 8420.0 in multi-core Geekbench, and 23029.39 in PassMark CPU. Cryptographic and vector computation benefits from hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory bandwidth delivers 98.09 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 43.54 GB/sec for large writes, though the composite PassMark memory score remains in the lower quartile.

Without integrated local NVMe drives, the ecs.c5.8xlarge trades local I/O speed for flexible architecture design, pairing dedicated CPU cores with standard network storage. In cost-efficiency terms, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio minimizes memory overhead expenditure for tasks requiring high thread counts without large in-memory caches. This technical profile fits multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving clusters, batch image processing, ray tracing pipelines, and distributed application tiers that scale horizontally across dedicated compute threads.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, the configuration delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server features 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and no GPU hardware. Performance metrics indicate weak single-thread performance alongside consistent mid-tier multi-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8420.0 and PassMark CPU score of 23029.39. Hardware-level support includes AVX-512F and AES instructions, while Redis SET throughput achieves 23.06 million operations per second. With its compute-oriented resource density and lack of local NVMe storage, this instance provides cost-efficient parallel processing suited for distributed batch jobs, static web serving fleets, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
